thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for dedicated pool `eu-west-2-dp-78` (model redwood-13b-quant). Observed p99 ~1.5s, p95 ~520ms, streaming stalls increasing. Affected routes: /v1/generate-stream, /v1/chat/stream. Queue depth rising ~120% above baseline.

mika (oncall): ack. Paging SRE. Is this localized to one pool or multi-pool?

sam (sre): I'm on it. Initial look: autoscaler logs show delayed slot handshake during warmup for dp-78; warmup success rate dropped. Querying metrics now for warmup latency and slot readiness.

jun (runtime): adding context — we've been seeing higher cold KV-cache misses for long-seq workloads, increased GPU warmup kernel compile times for this model (quant path). Could be compounding autoscale time.

taylor (dedicated-eng): FYI we pushed a config change to warmup concurrency last night in eu-west to reduce inference jitter. Might be interacting with the autoscaler ramp logic. I can roll back if needed.

olga (support): We have open tickets from two enterprise customers reporting streaming timeouts and partial responses: AcmeCorp (inc 8942) and Finori (inc 8928). Both on dedicated pools in eu-west-2. Customers seeing 5xx or stalled websockets.

pagerduty-bot: @mika assigned incident to escalation policy "dedicated-pools-paging". Severity: SEV2.

mika (oncall): Sam, prioritize queue depth -> backlog -> warmup timeline. If autoscaler taking >60s to make slots ready, we need manual mitigation.

sam (sre): Running quick PromQL for queue depth and warmup latency:

```
max_over_time(dedicated_pool_queue_depth{pool="dp-78"}[5m])
avg_over_time(warmup_slot_ready_seconds{pool="dp-78"}[5m])
```

Results: queue depth spiked to ~320, warmup_slot_ready_seconds median = 48s, 95th = 92s. Slot handshake failures (handshake_timeout) increased from 0.2% -> 6% in last 10m.

jun (runtime): That matches the compile-heavy warmup hypothesis. Kernel cache misses + JIT path warming. If autoscaler waits for a full warmup before marking slot ready we get backlog. Suggest marking slot ready earlier with restricted concurrency to accept lightweight traffic, then let runtime finish heavier compile async.

taylor (dedicated-eng): We can flip a flag to accept early-ready slots: `--accept-early-ready`. It reduces SLA risk if we limit concurrent requests per slot. Propose: enable early-ready + cap concurrency=1 for new slots in dp-78.

sam (sre): Agreed as short-term mitigation. Also: increase max-pool-size by +2 slots from reserved capacity to drain backlog while warmup finishes. Manual scale + route.

ivy (prod): Can we route traffic to backup pool in eu-west-3 for the two affected customers? They have cross-region redundancy enabled but not live by default. What's the risk of failover?

taylor (dedicated-eng): Failover is supported. But two notes: (1) model variant parity — eu-west-3 has `redwood-13b-quant-v2` which has slightly different latency profile, (2) there will be increased egress and potential auth config change. We can do a targeted route for AcmeCorp and Finori if they opt in.

olga (support): Reached out to AcmeCorp contact — they want immediate mitigation. Finori asked to be notified before failover.

sam (sre): Running mitigation steps now: 1) enable `--accept-early-ready` for dp-78 2) set new-slot-concurrency=1 3) manual scale +2 slots 4) temporary priority routing to new slots for buffered requests. Executing commands.

```
# internal tool
redctl pools update dp-78 --flags accept-early-ready=true --new-slot-concurrency=1
redctl pools scale dp-78 --delta 2 --reason "incident 3467890123"
```

sam (sre): Commands applied. Watching metrics.

(2 minutes later)

sam (sre): Metrics update: queue depth dropping ~40%, warmup ready 95th down to 35s, p99 falling toward 800ms. Streaming stalls still present but less frequent.

mika (oncall): Good progress. Continue monitoring for 15m. Sam, confirm if any customer-visible errors persist.

olga (support): AcmeCorp reports partial improvement, still occasional short stalls but no full timeouts. Finori still seeing stalls; they requested we hold off on cross-region failover.

jun (runtime): I'll open a follow-up to adjust compile cache priming for this model in eu-west-2 — preprime common kernels during low traffic windows. Also we'll add telemetry to see which requests cause the heavy compile.

taylor (dedicated-eng): I'll prepare a revert plan for last night's warmup concurrency config in case we see regressions. For now, keeping early-ready on.

sam (sre): Noted an increase in handshake retries from a particular node set (hostnames node-auk-xx). I'm triggering a graceful drain for 2 hosts to see if bad host is causing handshake failures.

```
kubectl cordon node-auk-12
kubectl drain node-auk-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

sam (sre): Drained one node, replacing it via autoscaler. Handshake failures metric dropped.

pagerduty-bot: Acknowledged. Notification sent to escalation channel.

mika (oncall): Handoff summary for next oncall (2nd shift):
- Incident 3467890123: p99 spike caused by autoscaler warmup delays + kernel compile cold path.
- Immediate actions taken: enabled early-ready slots (cap concurrency=1), scaled pool +2, drained suspect host node-auk-12, contacted customers.
- Current status: queue depth decreasing, p99 improved from 1.5s -> ~750ms, customers seeing partial improvement.
- Follow-ups: preprime kernels, evaluate warmup concurrency rollback, add early-ready as temporary playbook option, investigate autoscaler handshake timeout root cause.

mika (oncall): Paging @taylor for engineering follow-up and @jun for runtime follow-up. Leaving incident in monitoring state. If p99 back above 1.0s or queue depth rises >80% of peak, escalate to SEV1.

taylor (dedicated-eng): I'll own the warmup-concurrency revert plan and a playbook entry for `--accept-early-ready`.

jun (runtime): I'll own the compile priming task and add telemetry.

olga (support): I'll follow up with customers and update their tickets.

sam (sre): Monitoring until stable. Will escalate if any regression.

mika (oncall): Thanks team. Closing active paging. Will update incident record and link postmortem once we have RCA. :thumbsup:
